scope: Active terrain assets, production/terrain-reference scenes, local terrain authoring sources, terrain docs/evidence and retained transfer inputs; excludes standalone historical projects and external backups.
classification_intent: Proposed storage classes; currently tracked files remain ordinary Git. No imported asset is cleared for removal by this static audit.

rules.GIT_RUNTIME_TEXT: Keep native text assets and metadata in ordinary Git.
rules.GIT_REFERENCE_SCENE: Keep active dressing/performance reference scenes and metadata in ordinary Git.
rules.LFS_RUNTIME_BINARY: Keep at the identical Unity path; candidate for exact-path LFS conversion.
rules.GIT_EDITOR_CONTRACT: Keep source manifests and active editor map contracts in ordinary Git.
rules.LFS_EDITOR_MAP: Keep active editor map payloads accessible; candidate for exact-path LFS.
rules.LFS_EDITOR_CONTRACT: Keep large sealed manifests at the identical path; candidate for exact-path LFS.
rules.ARCHIVE_GATED_SOURCE: Archive candidate only after validator/rebuild restore contract passes.
rules.ARCHIVE_GATED_SCENE: Retained candidate scene; archive only with builder/test path compatibility.
rules.GIT_EVIDENCE: Keep canonical notes and small provenance/verification receipts in Git.
rules.ARCHIVE_GATED_EVIDENCE: Bulk evidence; archive after receipt links and consumers resolve.
rules.LOCAL_ONLY: Preserve locally; no Git, LFS or cloud publication.
rules.REVIEW_KEEP: Keep in current location until additional dependencies are resolved.

declared_sha256_locations: Existing sealed source manifests and their protected_files entries; not duplicated in the inventory.
limitations: GUID scan covers YAML serialized text; binary external-reference graph is not parsed.
TerrainData/layers/render textures conservatively kept; fresh Unity dependency proof is a migration gate.
Declared SHA256 values come from sealed manifests, not a fresh full payload rehash.
Whole-owner protection means ARCHIVE_GATED files are not safe to remove now.
Git blob IDs describe committed bytes; local-only files have no fresh content hashes.
This is a non-atomic disk inventory; start/end HEAD and errors are recorded.
